- If sentiment is positive (≥0.33) in recent history, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- If model shows a sharp spike followed by a forecast drop, it often overcorrects; cap the drop to avoid overshoot.  
- When true outcome is consistently lower than forecast (especially in early 30d window), model exhibits mean reversion bias; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for next period.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00) and forecast is high, model may be overconfident; reduce forecast by 1–2% if recent history shows no upward momentum.  
- For 30d forecasts, if first 5–7 days are overestimated, apply a “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for each of the first 5 days.  
- If sentiment history shows no positive sentiment, avoid forecasting upward trends; default to conservative mean of recent 7–10 days.
